title: Overloaded defenders

D0.outcome: Explains that a defender with two duties can be beaten by attacking one so the other is abandoned.

D1.outcome: When told 'find the overloaded piece', finds the piece and the capture or check that exploits it.

D2.outcome: In mixed sets, finds the overload that wins material, and does not play it when the two duties lie on one line or can be met by one move.

D3.outcome: Lists every duty of a defender before concluding it is overloaded, and predicts how an interposition or a third defender removes the effect.

misconceptions: A piece that defends two things is always overloaded.
sources: sources/sheets/edlasker_chess-strategy.md §4 K3 (ii) (a defender forced away by a bigger threat; a mate threat ties down a piece)
conditions: Both duties are needed at once and cannot be met by one move.
The attacker's exploiting move forces a decision (a capture or check) rather than merely hinting.
contrasts: Both duties lie on the same line, so one move of the defender serves both.
An interposition meets the second threat without moving the defender.
A piece with two jobs whose second job is not needed in this position.

soft_prereq_notes.SAF.COUNT.D2: the count shows where one defender has two jobs
